Create an array stream from an R function

Source: R/array-stream.R
function_array_stream.Rd

The function is called once for each requested array. It should return an object coercible by as_nanoarrow_array(), or NULL to indicate end of stream. The schema is required because it is available before the first array is requested. Neither construction nor schema access calls fun. After NULL or an error is returned, the callback is not called again.

Usage

function_array_stream(fun, schema, validate = TRUE)

Arguments

fun

A function called with no arguments to produce each array.

schema

A schema coercible by as_nanoarrow_schema(), used to coerce and validate each result.

validate

A single TRUE or FALSE. Use FALSE to skip validation within the callback. The stream's get_next() method can validate the returned array independently.

Value

An nanoarrow_array_stream

Details

Errors and interrupts raised by fun are converted to stream errors. Evaluation is also isolated in a top-level R context so other non-local exits (for example, invoking an abort restart) cannot escape through the C stream interface. Calling handlers in the caller are therefore not applied to callback evaluation. The callback is evaluated only on R's main thread. Warnings are handled in this isolated context, unless handled within fun. fun must not release the stream (or call its methods) while it is being evaluated. The stream retains fun until it is released; explicitly release streams when fun or its environment refers to the stream itself.

Examples

i <- 0L
stream <- function_array_stream(
  function() {
    i <<- i + 1L
    if (i > 2L) NULL else mtcars[i, , drop = FALSE]
  },
  infer_nanoarrow_schema(mtcars)
)
as.data.frame(stream$get_next())
#>   mpg cyl disp  hp drat   wt  qsec vs am gear carb
#> 1  21   6  160 110  3.9 2.62 16.46  0  1    4    4
as.data.frame(stream$get_next())
#>   mpg cyl disp  hp drat    wt  qsec vs am gear carb
#> 1  21   6  160 110  3.9 2.875 17.02  0  1    4    4
stream$get_next()
#> NULL
stream$release()
